Subject: Invoice delivery options / who sends invoices?

Hi Rafael,

Quick intro – I manage AP for ACME Retail. We're finalizing Redwood in our supplier ledger and have a couple of questions before we commit portal enrollment:

- Who will be the invoice originator in your system (Redwood accounting vs Redwood legal entity)?
- We prefer portal enrollment but need a signed PDF fallback for our internal audit for the first 90 days. Is that possible?
- VAT evidence: we need the invoice to include buyer VAT ID and a clear VAT line (reverse-charge if applicable).
- Can you provide a sample XML payload so our ERP team can validate the mapping?

Thanks — can you loop in whoever owns invoice creation?

Regards,
Linda Park
AP Director, ACME Retail
ap@acme-retail.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery options / who sends invoices?

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Invoice originator: Redwood Finance (Redwood Inference, Inc.) will be the legal issuer for hosted customers by default. We can route the "bill-from" header if you need a specific entity on the PDF.

2) Delivery options (we offer three):
   • Portal primary (recommended): we push invoices to an AP portal; you get a tokenized secure copy and webhook/ftp options.
   • Signed-PDF fallback: we can configure an automated signed PDF (ephemeral token / signed hash) for 90 days while AP completes portal onboarding.
   • Batch SFTP push: monthly batch (XML + zipped PDFs) for customers who prefer file drops.

3) VAT evidence: we include buyer VAT ID, VAT breakdown per line, and a metadata field indicating reverse-charge when applicable. We keep VAT tags in the XML and on the PDF.

I'm attaching: sample_invoice_v2.pdf, invoice_xml_schema_v2.xml, and a short portal_enroll_steps.pdf that shows the sequence for enrollment and role invites.

Can you confirm which delivery option you prefer and whether your ERP needs PO on the filename or inside the XML? If you prefer portal, we'll kick off the enrollment and share a token for onboarding.

Action I'm taking: the team will hold a quick mapping call with your ERP team (copying Kimberly to help with VAT mapping).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
(Attachment: sample_invoice_v2.pdf, invoice_xml_schema_v2.xml, portal_enroll_steps.pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Invoice delivery options / who sends invoices?

Hi Linda / Rafael — a couple of compliance notes from finance/ops perspective: 

- For EU VAT rules (reverse-charge) we'll need: buyer VAT ID on the header, explicit statement on the PDF and XML that reverse-charge applies, and a tax code in the XML so you can reconcile automatically.
- Retention and audit: we'll keep signed-PDFs for 365 days in the portal audit log, but we can enable a 90-day signed-PDF fallback window if that helps your AP onboarding timeline.
- PO handling: many ERP teams prefer PO as a header field in the XML and also embedded on the PDF filename (e.g., INV-12345_PO-9876.pdf). We can support both; let us know which you prefer.
- If ACME needs an invoice with the billing entity "Redwood Inference EMEA" instead of Redwood Inference, Inc., we can produce that variant but will need a signed reseller/contract addendum to change legal issuer.

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance Operations — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
